record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendix.
record.tranche_reason: Tests the difficulty of overfitting datasets that normally generalize using a modified gradient objective, and compares natural images with noise; this is a different method from fitting random labels with standard training.
record.gate_note: Reports outcomes for gradient-splitting objectives on CIFAR10 and Gaussian noise, plus a standard-training comparison. Cited results from other studies are not included as rows. Figure-only curves do not support exact numeric values.
record.test_reason: The study deliberately induces overfitting by optimizing against a designated test set. Its standard-training comparator reports natural-label generalization, but it does not test whether the same training recipe fits fixed random labels while producing chance held-out accuracy. The noise experiments also use the induced-overfitting objective. These results do not test V1's coexistence claim or any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the empirical conclusion: the same model can be deliberately made to overfit a dataset it normally generalizes, but finding such parameters requires more training; noise and dataset size alter that difficulty. It omits the authors' theoretical conclusion that gradient descent favors stable configurations that generalize when training and test data share invariants, and their claim of global optimality with respect to eventual stability under random initialization.
record.recipe_differences: Uses custom objectives that explicitly incorporate test-set loss or accuracy, rather than the standard training recipe used in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Objective function; dataset type (CIFAR10 versus Gaussian noise); dataset size; Softmax transformation for ResNet18 noise memorization.

fits_no_version.finding: An objective using test loss produces above 90% training accuracy and 2.4% designated-test accuracy; standard training reaches approximately 60% test accuracy at 90% training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A network that normally generalizes on natural images can be deliberately trained to overfit those images by changing its objective.

fits_no_version.finding: Under an objective constraining test accuracy, noise is easier to memorize; increasing dataset size makes noise overfitting easier and natural-image overfitting harder in the tested networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The optimization difficulty of deliberately induced overfitting depends on dataset structure, dataset size, and training configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: The paper offers a theoretical connection between parameter stability and input stability, and reports first-layer gradient norms for standard versus split-objective training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter stability may help explain generalization under the paper's assumptions; gradient norms provide a separate descriptive comparison.

record.problems: The central overfitting intervention uses test-set loss or accuracy in the training objective. Most curve values are figure-only, and the text reports no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible result rows identified.

untested.parts: Coexistence of near-perfect fixed-random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and chance random-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and training recipe.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with measured generalization gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The induced-overfitting findings neither support nor challenge V1. The unseen-holdout experiment described near Figure 1 still induces memorization through a split training objective. The stability argument does not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking performance. No omitted result directly testing a listed version was identified.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test small Inception, AlexNet, MLPs, or ImageNet; does not test random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same standard recipe.
Does not compare convolutional with fully connected architectures.
Uses Adam in experiments but does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD.
Discusses stability theoretically but does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with generalization gaps.
